title: State Visibility

bodyMarkdown:
## Definition

State visibility is the degree to which users can determine what the system is currently doing without active investigation or navigation away from the current task. It includes operational mode, active conditions, fault states, readiness level, and the status of the components the system is managing.

State visibility is a prerequisite for action. Users who cannot read system state cannot know whether to act, how to act, or whether a prior action had the intended effect. In high-consequence and time-pressured contexts, state visibility is the condition that makes correct operational decisions possible.

## Meaning in Creative Navy's documentation

In Creative Navy's documentation, state visibility refers to the interface property that makes current system condition legible at the point of use. The term is applied to complex systems such as medical devices, maritime vessels, industrial control systems, and multi-role enterprise platforms.

State visibility becomes an architectural problem when a system has many simultaneously active states across multiple components. In those contexts, the interface must maintain a legible picture of the system without overloading users with detail that they are not currently using.

## What effective state visibility includes

Effective state visibility requires readability under operating conditions. State indicators must remain communicable under divided attention, time pressure, variable lighting, physical movement, and gloved-hand use. A state indicator that is readable in a quiet office may be unreadable under operating theatre lighting or on a rolling vessel in heavy weather.

Effective state visibility requires spatial consistency. State indicators must remain in the same spatial position across view changes, modes, and workflow transitions. Spatial memory makes glance-readable state possible; if indicators move, users must search for state information at the moment they most need it.

Effective state visibility requires redundant communication channels. Critical state should be communicated through multiple simultaneous channels such as spatial position, icon form, and colour. Redundancy prevents the failure of a single channel from removing the signal under variable lighting, noise, vibration, or other degrading conditions.

## How state visibility differs from related terms

State visibility is not the same as operational clarity. Operational clarity is broader: it concerns whether users can understand information and act on it without unnecessary cognitive translation. State visibility is the subset that concerns what the system is currently doing. A system with good state visibility communicates current condition clearly; operational clarity also requires the communication to be organised into an appropriate hierarchy for decisions.

State visibility is not the same as data availability. A system can hold complete state data and still have poor state visibility if that data is buried in a secondary screen or depends on a single communication channel that fails under operating conditions.

State visibility is not a status bar, dashboard, or specific user-interface component. An interface can contain a dedicated status bar and still have poor state visibility if the bar sits outside the primary visual field, fails under divided attention, or depends only on colour.

## Examples of device state, information state, and transaction state

The Torqeedo maritime HMI case illustrates device and component state visibility in a multi-component energy system. Propulsion, battery, and generation state were unified into a single coherent display with stable spatial positions and synchronised update cadences. The case evidence records 50% faster energy state identification in a controlled experiment with 24 subjects, and glance reduction during manoeuvres in eye tracking with 7 subjects during sea trials.

The Kardion MCS Controller case illustrates clinical state visibility through layout stability. The layout stability standard specified that no element shifts position across any view transition. The rationale was that surgeons build spatial memory during procedures and depend on stable positions for rapid state verification. The available evidence is formative evaluation only; summative validation is the manufacturer's responsibility.

The deSoutter Medical case illustrates redundant non-colour cues for critical device states. Critical states used spatial position, icon form, and colour because variable theatre lighting can degrade single-channel colour communication. Most of the 6 benchmarked comparable devices relied on colour as the primary state indicator. This evidence is surgeon-reported from design review sessions.

KISPE Space illustrates information state as separate from device state. The interface made visible the state of the information itself, including where a record came from, how old it was, whether it was delivered, and whether the user could see it. Status was specified as seven independent dimensions rather than one green-to-red health score, because the single-score alternative would make identical colours carry conflicting meanings across domains. KISPE Space has no AI in this account; the unknowns are properties of sources, links, protocols, and sensors.

Schone Airspace Group illustrates transaction state as a third kind of state alongside device state and information state. A command in flight has its own lifecycle: requested, acknowledged, and executed or not. That lifecycle is neither the state of the aircraft nor the state of the data about it. The interface preserves command transaction semantics as a visible object so an operator can distinguish what has been asked, what has been acknowledged, and what has been observed to happen.

A European vendor of maritime traffic monitoring, inland navigation, and communications software for port authorities, coastal administrations, and waterway operators illustrates state visibility for system knowledge. The selected model kept vessel identity, tracked object, and timestamped observations as separate objects rather than collapsing them into a single resolved vessel record. Association status was expressed as resolved, unresolved, changed, or unknown, so the display showed not only what was known but how it was known and how firmly.

## Evidence basis

The strongest outcome evidence listed for state visibility is from the Torqeedo maritime HMI case: 50% faster energy state identification in a controlled experiment with 24 subjects, plus glance reduction during manoeuvres in eye tracking with 7 subjects during sea trials.

The Kardion MCS Controller evidence is formative only. The documented design requirement concerns layout stability for clinical state visibility, but summative validation remains the manufacturer's responsibility.

The deSoutter Medical evidence is surgeon-reported from design review sessions. The case supports the rationale for redundant non-colour cues under variable theatre lighting, but it is not presented as a measured outcome.

KISPE Space, Schone Airspace Group, and the maritime VTS engagement illustrate designed state models. The design decisions describe what was specified or designed; they do not establish measured results.

## Boundaries and limits

State visibility should not be treated as proof that an interface is operationally clear. Operational clarity includes state visibility but also requires appropriate information hierarchy for the decisions that need to be made.

State visibility should not be inferred from the presence of a dashboard, status bar, colour code, or complete internal data model. The interface must surface state in a way that remains readable under actual operating conditions.

The KISPE Space product was built, but Creative Navy did not support the build and has not compared the built interface against the delivered designs. The Schone Airspace Group product was built and is in test, not deployed. For KISPE Space, Schone Airspace Group, and the maritime VTS engagement, the state-visibility examples describe design decisions rather than measured effects.

## Related pages

Operational clarity is the closest related glossary term because it covers the broader question of whether users can understand information and act on it without unnecessary cognitive translation. State visibility is the more specific question of whether users can determine what the system is currently doing.

The Kardion, KISPE Space, Schone Airspace Group, and maritime VTS case pages are relevant examples because each shows a different form of state that an interface may need to make visible.
